article.title: Silver Bulletin pollster ratings 2024 archive
article.subtitle: The June 2024 version of the Silver Bulletin pollster ratings we used for our 2024 presidential election forecast.

extraction.summary: Archived June 12, 2024 version of the Silver Bulletin pollster ratings used in the 2024 presidential forecast. Silver says the ratings restore the methodology he used at FiveThirtyEight when he left in 2023, with no methodological changes, and add only 63 new polls from the 2023 gubernatorial races, congressional special elections and the 2024 Republican primaries. The article defines the table's columns: letter grade, predictive plus-minus (historical accuracy plus a transparency bonus), mean-reverted bias, and number of polls. It also reports that 2024 GOP primary polls missed the margin by 9.7 points on average with a 4.4-point pro-Trump bias. The first page of the ratings table gives example values for the top pollsters.

findings.statement: The June 2024 Silver Bulletin pollster ratings restore the methodology Silver used for FiveThirtyEight pollster ratings when he left in 2023, with no methodological changes, only new data.
findings.rationale: Silver says he continues to own the IP for the original FiveThirtyEight models.
findings.evidence_quote: These ratings restore the methodology that I used for pollster ratings when I left FiveThirtyEight in 2023

findings.statement: The Silver Bulletin 2024 presidential forecast uses the pollster ratings, which were recalculated in preparation for the forecast's launch.
findings.evidence_quote: I've recalculated the pollster ratings that the model employs

findings.statement: The June 2024 ratings update added polls from the 2023 gubernatorial elections, congressional special elections and the 2024 Republican presidential primaries. This came to only 63 new polls, so the ratings changed little.

quantities.name: new polls added since last update

findings.rationale: Most of these elections were uncompetitive and lightly polled.
findings.evidence_quote: only 63 polls since the last update. So the ratings have not changed very much.

findings.statement: The 2024 Democratic presidential primaries were excluded entirely from the pollster ratings. There were few polls, the New Hampshire polls involved Biden as a write-in candidate, and named candidates (Phillips, Williamson) often ran behind 'uncommitted'. Few if any of these polls would meet Silver's rules for primary polls.
findings.rationale: Write-in races are a difficult circumstance that Silver does not think is fair to judge pollsters on.
findings.evidence_quote: Few if any of these polls would qualify by the various rules I apply to primary polls, so I just skipped the Democratic primaries entirely.

findings.statement: Eligible polls in the 2024 Republican presidential primaries missed the final margin between the top two candidates by an average of 9.7 percentage points. This is consistent with the long-term average presidential primary poll error since 2000 of 9.3 points.

quantities.name: 2024 presidential primary average absolute error
quantities.context: margin between the top two candidates

quantities.name: long-term primary poll average error since 2000

findings.evidence_quote: missed the final margin between the top two candidates by an average of 9.7 percentage points

findings.statement: 2024 Republican primary polls had a pro-Trump bias, overestimating Trump's margin over Nikki Haley by an average of 4.4 points.

quantities.name: pro-Trump bias
quantities.context: 2024 GOP primaries, Trump vs. Haley margin

findings.evidence_quote: overestimating Trump's margin against Nikki Haley by an average of 4.4 points

findings.statement: Each pollster receives an overall letter grade derived from its predictive plus-minus rating.
findings.evidence_quote: An overall grade based on a pollster's predictive plus-minus rating.

findings.statement: Grades for pollsters with sparse data are rounded to a combined grade, e.g. 'A/B' rather than 'A-'. In the table, A/B pollsters have roughly 13-29 polls.

quantities.name: poll counts of A/B-graded pollsters in table
quantities.context: read from page 1 of the table

findings.rationale: Sparse data warrants a less precise grade.
findings.evidence_quote: Grades for pollsters with sparse data are rounded (e.g. to "A/B" rather than A-)

findings.statement: Banned pollsters automatically receive a grade of F regardless of their plus-minus score. For example, Strategic Vision LLC has a predictive plus-minus of -0.38, which would otherwise be good, but is graded F.
findings.evidence_quote: banned pollsters automatically receive a grade of F

findings.statement: Banned/unbanned decisions in the June 2024 ratings were reverted to those in place in spring 2023.
findings.rationale: Silver did not want to re-litigate them.
findings.evidence_quote: I'm also reverting back any banned/unbanned decisions to the ones that were in place in spring 2023.

findings.statement: Predictive plus-minus is the expected future accuracy of a pollster, combining its historical accuracy with its transparency/disclosure standards. Negative scores are better and mean the pollster is expected to be more accurate than average.
findings.evidence_quote: Negative plus-minus scores are good and imply that we expect the pollster to be more accurate than average going forward.

findings.statement: Pollsters receive a transparency bonus in predictive plus-minus if they are members of the AAPOR Transparency Initiative or share their data with the Roper Center archive.
findings.evidence_quote: pollsters get a bonus if they're either a member of the AAPOR Transparency Initiative or share their data with the Roper Center archive

findings.statement: Mean-reverted bias is a pollster's historical average statistical bias toward Democrats or Republicans, shrunk toward zero based on the number of polls in the database. 'D +1.5' means the pollster has historically overrated Democratic candidates.
findings.rationale: Shrinkage reduces noise for pollsters with few polls.
findings.evidence_quote: reverted to a mean of zero based on the number of polls in the database

findings.statement: Mean-reverted bias is calculated only for races in which exactly one Republican and one Democrat are the two leading candidates, so it excludes presidential primaries.
findings.rationale: Partisan bias is undefined without a D-vs-R matchup.
findings.evidence_quote: This is calculated only for races in which exactly one Republican and one Democrat are the two leading candidates

findings.statement: The pollster ratings database goes back to 1998. Polls from more recent years are weighted more heavily.
findings.evidence_quote: The database goes back to 1998, though polls from more recent years are weighted more heavily.

findings.statement: In general, the pollster ratings cover all polls conducted in the 21 days before presidential, congressional and gubernatorial general elections, and before presidential primaries.
findings.evidence_quote: these ratings cover all polls in the 21 days prior to presidential, Congressional and gubernatorial general elections, and presidential primaries

findings.statement: The raw poll dataset (Rawpolls 061224) contains topline numbers from more than 11,500 polls and is free to use with attribution. A separate file (Pollster Stats Full 2024) gives detailed per-pollster stats, including race-call rates and alternative plus-minus calculations.
findings.evidence_quote: including topline numbers from more than 11,500 polls

findings.statement: Top of the June 2024 ratings table (grade, predictive +/-, mean-reverted bias, number of polls): Selzer A+ -1.27 D+0.1 54; NYT/Siena A+ -1.18 D+1.0 95; ABC/WaPo A+ -0.94 D+0.8 90; Research & Polling A+ -0.92 R+0.5 44; SurveyUSA A -0.86 +0.0 857; Siena College A -0.84 R+0.2 63; Marquette A/B -0.81 D+0.2 15; AtlasIntel A -0.75 D+0.2 24; Marist A -0.70 D+0.3 200; Monmouth A -0.62 D+2.0 123; Emerson A- -0.56 D+0.3 264; PPP A- -0.39 D+0.9 463; Mason-Dixon A- -0.38 R+0.5 446; Quinnipiac A- -0.38 D+0.5 222.

Grade thresholds can be approximated from page 1 of the table. A+ appears for plus-minus up to about -0.92, A for roughly -0.86 to -0.62, and A- from about -0.58 to -0.38. The cutoffs are not stated in the text.
The ratings table has 21 pages of roughly 25 rows each, implying roughly 500 rated pollsters.

political_insights.insight: Presidential primary polls are far less accurate than general election polls, missing the top-two margin by about 9-10 points on average.
political_insights.evidence: 9.7 points in the 2024 GOP primaries; 9.3 points on average since 2000.
political_insights.forecasting_implication: Primary forecasts need much wider uncertainty than general election forecasts.

political_insights.insight: 2024 GOP primary polls overstated Trump's margin over Haley.
political_insights.forecasting_implication: Frontrunner margins in primary polls may be overstated.

open_questions: Exact formula combining historical accuracy and the transparency bonus into predictive plus-minus, and the size of the bonus.
Functional form and strength of mean reversion for bias as a function of poll count.
Recency weighting scheme across years since 1998.
Exact grade cutoffs and the threshold for 'sparse data' rounded grades.
The rules used to qualify primary polls.
How the ratings translate into poll weights and house effects in the 2024 presidential model's polling averages.
